issues.legal_issue: Fraudulent misrepresentation about the character of a document makes the resulting transaction void when the signer did not intend to enter into that transaction.
material_facts: The illiterate signer intended to execute a gift deed in favour of her daughter and believed that the thumb impressions she made related to that deed alone.
She was unaware that she had also executed a sale deed in favour of others and did not intend to enter into that sale transaction.
The parties did not dispute the manner in which the documents were executed.
issues.conclusion: The sale transaction was wholly void, rather than merely voidable, because the misrepresentation concerned the character of the document and the signer never intended to enter into that transaction.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Ningawwa v. Byrappa, and the distinction it draws between misrepresentation about a document's character and misrepresentation about its contents or legal effect, misrepresentation about character makes the transaction void where the signer's mind did not accompany the signature. Fraud generally makes a transaction voidable, but this category of misrepresentation is an exception. The Court also referred to Foster v. Mackinon in explaining that principle.

predicates.document_execution_dispute: A party challenges the legal effect of a document that the party signed or executed.
predicates.misrepresented_document_character: Another person led the signer to believe that the document was of a different kind from the document actually executed.
predicates.signer_did_not_intend_transaction: The signer did not intend to enter into the transaction embodied in the document actually executed.
predicates.transaction_void: The transaction embodied in the document is wholly void.

issues.definition: When a document-execution dispute involves deception about the kind of document and the signer did not intend its transaction, the transaction is wholly void.

issues.legal_issue: A civil suit to cancel a void transaction concerning land is barred when consolidation proceedings concerning that land are pending, because the transaction's validity can be determined in those proceedings.
material_facts: A suit was brought to cancel a sale deed concerning land.
The plaintiff's claim was that the sale transaction was void because she had been deceived about the character of the document and had not intended to enter into the sale.
Consolidation proceedings concerning the property were pending when the suit was brought.
issues.conclusion: The civil suit was not maintainable under Section 49 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953; the parties could seek appropriate relief from the consolidation authorities, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49 bars civil and revenue courts from deciding disputes that could or ought to be taken up under the consolidation legislation. Under Gorakh Nath Dube v. Hari Narain Singh, consolidation authorities can determine whether a transaction is void, while a civil suit may be needed to set aside a voidable document that remains effective until cancelled. Because the transaction here was void, its validity could be adjudicated by the consolidation authorities. Applying Ningawwa v. Byrappa, the misrepresentation about the document's character made the transaction void.

rule.if: civil_suit_to_cancel_document and consolidation_proceedings_pending and land_rights_dispute and transaction_void

predicates.civil_suit_to_cancel_document: A party brings a civil suit seeking cancellation of a document.
predicates.consolidation_proceedings_pending: Proceedings to consolidate landholdings are pending concerning the land at issue.
predicates.land_rights_dispute: The dispute concerns rights or interests in land that are at issue in the consolidation proceedings.
predicates.transaction_void: The transaction embodied in the document is wholly void.
predicates.civil_suit_not_maintainable: The civil suit cannot be maintained to determine the dispute.

issues.definition: A civil suit to cancel a document concerning land cannot be maintained when consolidation proceedings concerning that land are pending and the dispute concerns a void transaction.
